The invention relates to an X-ray imaging apparatus (2), comprising: a source (4) for generating X-ray radiation, an object receiving space (6) for arranging an object of interest for X-ray imaging, an X-ray collimator arrangement (8) arranged between the source (4) and the collimator arrangement (8), and an X-ray mirror arrangement (10). Consequently, the X-ray intensity at the object receiving space (6) is increased. In order to limit the X-ray radiation to an area, where the X-ray radiation can be utilized form imaging, an angle of spread Θm between the mirrors (22) and a length LM of each mirror (22) is adapted, such that a number of total reflections of X-ray radiation, provided by the source (4), at the mirrors (22) is limited. The limitation provides the effect that an angle of reflection Θr of the totally reflected X-ray radiation is limited. Consequently, an X-ray intensity at the object receiving space (6) is increased while constrains are provided, which prevent a large increase of a width of the X-ray radiation provided at the object receiving space (6), which effectively improves an imaging quality of an object of interest being arrangeable at the object receiving space (6).

The invention relates to an X-ray imaging apparatus designed to improve the delivery and quality of X-ray radiation used for imaging an object. The apparatus includes an X-ray source for generating X-ray radiation, an object receiving space in which the object to be examined is positioned, a collimator arrangement for shaping or limiting the X-ray beam, and an X-ray mirror arrangement arranged between the X-ray source and the collimator arrangement.

In one embodiment, the X-ray mirror arrangement includes two tapered mirrors positioned opposite one another. These mirrors face each other and are configured to guide X-ray radiation emitted by the source toward the collimator arrangement. The tapered configuration helps direct the radiation efficiently along a desired path, thereby increasing the amount of useful X-ray radiation that reaches the object receiving space.

By concentrating or guiding the radiation more effectively, the mirror arrangement increases the X-ray intensity at the object receiving space. This can improve the efficiency of the imaging process, for example by enabling a stronger signal at the detector, reducing exposure time, or allowing operation with a lower output from the X-ray source while maintaining image quality.

The geometry of the mirror arrangement is selected carefully. In particular, the angle of spread between the opposing tapered mirrors and the length of the mirrors are adapted so as to limit the number of total reflections experienced by the X-ray radiation as it travels through the mirror arrangement. Controlling the number of reflections is important because each reflection influences the propagation direction and angular distribution of the beam.

By limiting the number of total reflections, the apparatus also restricts the reflection angle of the X-ray radiation. This prevents the beam from widening excessively before it reaches the collimator and the object receiving space. As a result, the X-ray beam remains better controlled and more precisely directed. This reduction in unwanted beam spreading contributes to improved imaging quality, for example by enhancing spatial resolution, reducing stray radiation, and providing a more uniform and accurately shaped beam for imaging.
outputs.L4:
An X-ray imaging apparatus includes an X-ray source, a collimator, and an imaging area in which an object to be examined is positioned. Between the X-ray source and the collimator, the apparatus is provided with a mirror arrangement designed to guide and concentrate X-ray radiation toward the object space. The mirror arrangement includes a pair of opposing tapered mirrors arranged so that the distance between their reflecting surfaces changes along the direction of X-ray travel. As radiation emitted from the X-ray source enters this mirror arrangement, at least a portion of the radiation is reflected by the tapered mirror surfaces and directed toward the region that will be imaged.

The geometry of the mirror arrangement is selected so that the X-ray beam is directed efficiently toward the imaging area without causing excessive beam divergence. In particular, the spread angle of the opposing tapered mirrors and the length of the mirror arrangement are controlled so as to limit the number of reflections experienced by the X-rays. By restricting excessive multiple reflections, the apparatus reduces losses that would otherwise occur due to absorption, scattering, or inefficient reflection at the mirror surfaces. At the same time, the mirrors help redirect X-rays that might otherwise travel outside the useful imaging path, thereby increasing the amount of radiation available for imaging the object.

The collimator positioned downstream of the mirror arrangement further defines the shape and size of the beam before it reaches the object space. Because the mirror arrangement has already guided a greater portion of the emitted radiation toward the desired direction, the collimator can form a useful imaging beam with improved intensity while avoiding unnecessary widening of the radiation field. This helps maintain a controlled exposure area and reduces irradiation of regions outside the object of interest.

As a result, the X-ray intensity in the object space is increased without excessively increasing the beam width. The apparatus can therefore deliver more usable X-ray radiation to the target region, improving image quality, contrast, and signal strength. By concentrating radiation on the object of interest and reducing wasted radiation outside the imaging area, the system enhances imaging efficiency and may also contribute to reduced exposure requirements for obtaining a diagnostically useful image.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical invention summary describing an X-ray imaging device with numbered components, including an X-ray mirror arrangement between the source and collimator that limits total reflections by adapting mirror length and spread angle.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Invention Summary

An X-ray imaging device is provided for generating an X-ray image of an object while improving beam conditioning efficiency and reducing unwanted radiation losses. The device comprises an X-ray source, an X-ray mirror arrangement positioned between the X-ray source and a collimator, and an X-ray detector arranged downstream of the object to be imaged. The X-ray mirror arrangement is configured such that a total number of X-ray reflections occurring within the mirror arrangement is limited by adapting at least one of a mirror length and a spread angle of the reflected X-ray beam.

### Numbered Components

1. **X-ray Imaging Device**  
   The overall system configured to irradiate an object with X-rays and detect transmitted or scattered X-ray radiation for image generation.

2. **X-ray Source**  
   A radiation source configured to emit an X-ray beam, preferably a divergent X-ray beam, toward an imaging region. The X-ray source may comprise an X-ray tube, microfocus source, rotating anode source, or other suitable X-ray emitter.

3. **X-ray Beam**  
   Radiation emitted by the X-ray source and directed toward the object. The X-ray beam may include a range of propagation directions and may initially have a comparatively large angular spread.

4. **X-ray Mirror Arrangement**  
   An optical beam-conditioning arrangement disposed between the X-ray source and the collimator. The X-ray mirror arrangement is configured to reflect at least part of the emitted X-ray beam by grazing incidence reflection.

5. **Mirror Element**  
   One or more reflective surfaces of the X-ray mirror arrangement. Each mirror element may include a polished substrate and a reflective coating suitable for X-ray reflection, such as a metal coating, multilayer coating, or total external reflection surface.

6. **Mirror Length**  
   The effective reflective length of the mirror element along the propagation direction of the X-ray beam. The mirror length is selected or adapted such that X-rays undergo no more than a predetermined number of reflections within the mirror arrangement.

7. **Spread Angle**  
   The angular divergence or angular spread of the X-ray beam accepted by or output from the mirror arrangement. The spread angle is adapted in relation to the mirror length so that the total number of reflections of X-rays within the mirror arrangement remains limited.

8. **Reflection-Limiting Configuration**  
   A geometric configuration of the X-ray mirror arrangement in which the mirror length and the spread angle are mutually selected to restrict multiple reflections. In particular, the mirror arrangement may be designed so that substantially all reflected X-rays undergo only a limited number of reflections, for example one reflection or fewer than a predetermined maximum number of reflections.

9. **Collimator**  
   A beam-shaping component arranged downstream of the X-ray mirror arrangement. The collimator defines the spatial extent of the X-ray beam incident on the object and may comprise one or more apertures, slits, shutters, or adjustable collimating leaves.

10. **Imaging Region**  
   A region in which an object to be examined is positioned. The conditioned and collimated X-ray beam passes through or interacts with the object in this region.

11. **Object**  
   A subject, sample, patient, component, or material to be imaged by the X-ray imaging device.

12. **X-ray Detector**  
   A detector arranged downstream of the imaging region and configured to receive X-rays after interaction with the object. The detector converts received X-ray radiation into electrical signals representative of an X-ray image.

13. **Control Unit**  
   An optional electronic control system configured to control operation of the X-ray source, collimator, detector, and, where applicable, adjustable parameters of the X-ray mirror arrangement.

### Functional Description

During operation, the X-ray source emits an X-ray beam toward the X-ray mirror arrangement. The X-ray mirror arrangement reflects selected portions of the beam at grazing incidence and directs them toward the collimator. The collimator then shapes the beam before it enters the imaging region and irradiates the object. Radiation transmitted through or otherwise emerging from the object is detected by the X-ray detector to form image data.

The X-ray mirror arrangement is specifically positioned between the X-ray source and the collimator so that beam conditioning occurs before final collimation. By adapting the mirror length and/or the spread angle of the beam accepted or produced by the mirror arrangement, the geometry of the mirror arrangement limits the total number of reflections experienced by the X-rays. This reduces attenuation, spectral distortion, scattering, heat load, and imaging artifacts that may otherwise arise from excessive multiple reflections.

In one implementation, the mirror length is shortened relative to a beam divergence such that X-rays outside a desired angular range do not continue to undergo repeated reflections. In another implementation, the spread angle is reduced or selected so that only rays capable of reaching the collimator after a limited number of reflections are accepted. The mirror length and spread angle may also be jointly optimized so that the reflected beam has a desired intensity distribution while maintaining the reflection count below a predetermined threshold.

### Technical Effect

The invention provides an X-ray imaging device in which the X-ray mirror arrangement improves beam directionality and conditioning while avoiding excessive reflection events. Limiting the total number of reflections increases usable X-ray flux at the collimator, improves image quality, reduces unwanted background radiation, and enables more efficient operation of the X-ray imaging system.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention relating to X-ray imaging in formal patent language, focusing on how a mirror arrangement increases radiation intensity at an object receiving space without excessively widening the useful X-ray beam.
counterfactuals.output:
An X-ray imaging apparatus is provided comprising an X-ray source for emitting X-radiation, an object receiving space disposed in a beam path of the X-radiation, and an X-ray detector arranged to receive radiation transmitted through an object located in the object receiving space. A mirror arrangement is disposed between the X-ray source and the object receiving space and is configured to redirect at least a portion of the emitted X-radiation toward the object receiving space so as to increase radiation intensity incident upon the object.

The mirror arrangement comprises one or more X-ray reflective surfaces arranged at grazing incidence relative to the X-radiation. The reflective surfaces are shaped and oriented such that radiation which would otherwise propagate outside a useful imaging beam is deflected into, or maintained within, the useful beam directed toward the object receiving space. In this manner, the photon flux available for imaging is increased without requiring a corresponding increase in source power and without producing an excessive widening of the useful X-ray beam.

In one embodiment, the mirror arrangement includes a plurality of mirror elements positioned around a central beam axis extending from the X-ray source to the object receiving space. The mirror elements may be curved, tapered, or otherwise profiled to collect divergent X-radiation from the source and to reflect the collected radiation toward a predetermined cross-sectional region at the object receiving space. The predetermined region substantially corresponds to the desired imaging field, such that radiation intensity is enhanced over the object while stray radiation outside the imaging field is reduced.

The mirror arrangement may be configured so that the reflected radiation converges only partially, is substantially collimated, or is directed with a controlled divergence. Accordingly, the useful X-ray beam is intensified at the object receiving space while its lateral extent remains limited to a dimension suitable for imaging. The arrangement thereby avoids unnecessary irradiation of regions outside the object receiving space and reduces scatter that would otherwise degrade image quality.

The reflective surfaces may comprise materials or coatings suitable for X-ray reflection at grazing incidence, including multilayer coatings selected in accordance with the energy spectrum of the X-ray source. The mirror arrangement may be rotationally symmetric, polygonal, segmented, or formed as opposing mirror surfaces, depending on the desired beam geometry. In certain embodiments, the mirror arrangement is adjustable to vary the position, convergence, or angular distribution of the reflected radiation relative to the object receiving space.

By providing a mirror arrangement which redirects otherwise unused X-radiation into the useful beam, the apparatus achieves increased radiation intensity at the object receiving space while maintaining a controlled beam width. The invention is particularly advantageous in X-ray imaging systems requiring improved exposure efficiency, reduced acquisition time, or enhanced image signal without increasing patient dose outside the intended imaging region.

1. **An X-ray imaging apparatus**, comprising:  
   an **X-ray source** configured to emit X-ray radiation along an optical path toward an imaging region;  
   an **object space** disposed downstream of the X-ray source and configured to receive an object to be imaged;

   at least one **tapered X-ray mirror assembly** arranged along the optical path and configured to reflect X-rays at grazing incidence so as to control beam divergence, convergence, or spatial distribution.

2. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein the tapered X-ray mirror assembly comprises one or more reflecting surfaces extending over a **mirror length LM**, the mirror length LM defining an axial distance over which incident X-rays interact with the tapered reflective surface.

3. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein the tapered X-ray mirror assembly has a **mirror spread angle Θm**, the mirror spread angle Θm representing an angular taper or angular separation associated with the reflecting surface geometry, thereby determining a degree of beam spreading, focusing, or redirection imparted to the X-ray beam.

4. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein X-rays incident on the tapered X-ray mirror assembly are reflected at a **reflection angle Θr**, the reflection angle Θr being selected to satisfy a grazing-incidence reflection condition for the X-ray wavelength or energy range emitted by the X-ray source.

5. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein the **X-ray source** is configured to provide a divergent, quasi-parallel, or shaped X-ray beam, and wherein the tapered X-ray mirror assembly modifies the angular distribution of the beam before, within, or after passage through the object space.

6. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein the **object space** is positioned such that the object is irradiated by X-rays whose propagation direction or angular spread has been at least partially controlled by the tapered X-ray mirror assembly.

7. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein the **collimator** cooperates with the tapered X-ray mirror assembly to reduce stray radiation, define a field of view, select a portion of the emitted X-ray beam, or improve image contrast at an X-ray detector.

8. **The apparatus of claim 1**, wherein the **mirror spread angle Θm**, the **mirror length LM**, and the **reflection angle Θr** are selected in combination to provide a desired illumination condition in the object space, including at least one of beam expansion, beam compression, beam parallelization, beam focusing, or enhanced photon collection efficiency.

9. **The apparatus of claim 1**, further comprising an **X-ray detector** positioned downstream of the object space and configured to receive X-rays transmitted through, scattered by, or phase-shifted by the object, thereby generating image data corresponding to the object.

10. **In operation**, the X-ray source emits radiation toward the collimator, the collimator conditions the beam, the tapered X-ray mirror assembly reflects the conditioned beam at the reflection angle Θr over the mirror length LM, and the taper defined by the mirror spread angle Θm produces a controlled X-ray beam that irradiates the object space for acquisition of an X-ray image.
